claims: n228_S59604312.json is an exact rational certificate of 228 unit squares, each its centre (cx, cy) in [0, S]^2 and t = tan(theta/2), in a square of rational side S whose 12-place ceiling #984 prints as the bound, 15.596043120921; the issue also prints the exact side to 30 places, 15.596043120920791646977220704185..., and states that it is 0.008558354808882 below the registry's 15.60460147572967429 (T-174, Francisco Couzo, improved by PingYou Ltd), read at main fa980f8e. evidence/registration/n228.cert is the same packing as text (n S, then x y t per square). n228.strict.cert and n228.strict.json are the packing moved by (1e-15, 1e-15) in a square of side S + 2e-15, for checkers that need positive wall margins. The issue says the packing touches the four walls (wall margin exactly 0). Feasibility only: no optimality, KKT or rigidity claim.

The issue reports three checks, run by the author: the repository's frozen verifier verify.py (exact Fraction, separating axes, all 25878 pairs) VALID; search/indep_check.py (exact rational polygon clipping, 525 close pairs) PASSED; and search/fu_strict_check.py on the strict copy (four edge normals, positive wall margins) STRICT VALID, least pair margin 2.389e-10, least wall margin 1e-15. It says the first and third share the separating-axis method and the half-angle parametrisation, that the second and third were written by the agent that found the packing and the first fixed before the search, and that none is this registry's verifier. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.

The issue discloses first that the packing does not beat the Kaggle per-puzzle leaderboard's side-only entries at 228: 15.596043116631669919627353... (team Nevska, 8 November), 4.289e-09 below this side, and 15.596043116646272293906688... (team square1000, 29 October), 4.275e-09 below; neither supplies a packing. It says the open request #983 (15.600801734812, Doga Ozden) lies 0.004758613890 above this packing and that the two arrangements were not compared. Its lineage: Francisco Couzo's n = 404 packing as this registry retains it (couzo-issue763-2026-10-23, n404.cert), mirrored, every square with 13.8 <= x + y < 23.8 deleted and the rest moved by (-5, -5), removing five periods of the band; a penalty step and an exact-constraint sequential-LP polish give 15.597084912 (n228_S59708491.json, also certified), and basin hopping that re-seats cells at the band's ends (search/attack.py) gives the claimed side. It asks that Couzo's n = 404 packing be credited as the start and Roberto Ono as the credit name, and says the packing was found, certified and checked by an AI coding agent (Claude, by Anthropic) directed by a person.
